  "text": "Every Thursday, a staircase appeared behind the fishmonger's shop, leading down to the sea as it had been thirty years ago.

Elias found it while looking for a dropped coin.

At the bottom, his father sat on an overturned boat, repairing a net. He was younger than Elias now, with black hair and a thumbnail split down the middle.

“You're blocking the light,” his father said.

Elias stepped aside.

He returned the following Thursday with two sandwiches. His father accepted one without asking his name.

They ate, watching gulls gather around something neither could see.

For six weeks, Elias brought lunch. He learned that his father disliked fishing, wanted to visit Naples, and worried that his little boy was frightened of him.

“Are you unkind to him?” Elias asked.

“Sometimes I'm tired.”

The seventh Thursday, the staircase had only nine steps. Beyond the last, seawater moved through darkness.

His father was waiting on the boat.

“Next week I'll bring photographs,” Elias said. “There's someone you should see.”

His father held out the net.

“Take this end a moment.”

They worked until the light began to fail. Elias knew no knots, so his father showed him, patiently, twice.

When he climbed back, water covered his shoes.

The next Thursday, there was only a wall behind the shop.

Elias stood facing it with the photographs in his pocket. Then he walked home and called his son.

“Nothing's happened,” he said when the call connected. “I wondered if you'd had lunch.”

His son said he had.

Elias nearly said goodbye. Instead, he sat down at the kitchen table and asked what he'd eaten."
